test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 9 Sept 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In which of the following locations is the Brahmaputra river known as Tsang Po?
solution:
The correct answer is** __Tibet.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Yarlung Tsangpo**

 
 
• The upper stream of the **Brahmaputra River**, also known as the Yarlung Tsangpo or Yarlung Zangbo, can be found in **China's Tibet Autonomous Region.**
 
• It is the** fifth-longest **river in **China** and the longest in **Tibet**. Dangque Zangbu, which translates to "Horse River," is another name for the upper section.
 
• It began at the** Angsi Glacier in western Tibet**, southeast of **Mount Kailash** and **Lake Manasarovar**. From there, it created the **South Tibet Valley** and the Yarlung Tsangpo Grand Canyon before entering the Indian state of **Arunachal Pradesh.**
 
• **Nyangchu River, Lhasa River, Nyang River, and Parlung Tsangpo** are the primary tributaries of Yarlung Tsangpo.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Brahmaputra river**

 
 
• The Brahmaputra is a river that connects** Tibet, northeast India, and Bangladesh.** It is transboundary. It is also referred to as the **Jamuna River in Bangla**, the **Siang/Dihang River in Arunachali**, the **Luit in Assamese**, and the** Yarlung Tsangpo in Tibetan**. By discharge, it ranks** 9th largest and 15th longest** river in the world.
 
• The Yarlung Tsangpo River originates in the **Manasarovar Lake **region, near **Mount Kailash**, on the northern side of the Himalayas in Burang County, Tibet.
 
• It is not to be confused with the Indian Yamuna and flows south through Bangladesh as the** Jamuna**, passing through the** Assam Valley** in the southwest.
 
• It eventually joins the **Ganges**, which is commonly referred to as the **Padma in Bangladesh**, in the vast Ganges Delta, where it becomes the** Meghna** before draining into the** Bay of Bengal.**
